item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Sharif’s 2024 record is mixed but not empty: he clearly helped preserve regime objectives through coalition formation, IMF-backed stabilization, and structured external diplomacy. At the same time, domestic opposition management leaned heavily on coercion, censorship, and judicial pressure, which may have protected the coalition in the short run but weakened durable institutional legitimacy.

**Accepted Claims**
- **E0028 | Joint Statement on 6th Round of Pakistan-UK Dialogue on Arms Control & Non-Proliferation** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-05-16 | [link](https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/6th-round-of-pakistan-uk-dialogue-on-arms-control-non-proliferation) | Pakistan and the UK held a cordial arms-control/nonproliferation dialogue and pledged continued coordination in multilateral fora. This shows active management of a sensitive external relationship through institutions, not escalation. | 8B.9
- **E0019 | Pakistan-China Bilateral Consultations on Arms Control and Nonproliferation** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-09-14 | [link](https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/pakistan-china-bilateral-consultations-on-arms-control-and-nonproliferation) | Pakistan continued structured consultations with China on security, cyber, AI, outer space, and peaceful nuclear technology. That supports a reading of regime management through ongoing great-power coordination. | 8B.9
- **E0021 | The visit of UN Disarmament Fellows to Pakistan** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-10-21 | [link](https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/the-visit-of-un-disarmament-fellows-to-pakistan) | Pakistan briefed UN disarmament fellows on arms control, disarmament, nonproliferation, and nuclear safety architecture. This is evidence of institutional engagement and a disciplined external posture. | 8B.9
- **E0040 | Sharif urged India to engage in dialogue for resolution of J-K dispute** | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | [link](https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute) | Sharif publicly urged India into dialogue on Kashmir, which is the clearest de-escalatory move in the record. That supports crisis management through diplomacy rather than war. | 8B.9
- **E0058 | Peace in South Asia depends on settlement of Kashmir dispute** | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-21 | [link](https://www.radio.gov.pk/21-09-2024/peace-in-south-asia-depends-on-settlement-of-kashmir-dispute-pm) | Sharif framed regional security in terms of dialogue and peaceful settlement. This is direct evidence of trying to preserve stability and avoid unnecessary escalation. | 8B.9
- **E0060 | PM Shehbaz urges AJK govt political leadership to resolve issues through dialogue** | Radio Pakistan | 2024-05-12 | [link](https://www.radio.gov.pk/12-05-2024/pm-shehbaz-urges-ajk-govt-political-leadership-to-resolve-issues-through-dialogue) | During unrest in Azad Kashmir, Sharif directed local leaders to negotiate rather than coerce. This is a concrete example of crisis management through bargaining. | 8B.9
- **E0012 | UNGA remark urging dialogue on Kashmir** | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | [link](https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute) | The same UNGA intervention also contained clear de-escalatory language. It reinforces that Sharif used diplomacy as part of regime and security management. | 8B.9
- **E003 / E0310 / E0377 | IMF says growth returned, inflation fell, reserves rebuilt** | IMF | 2024-09-27 | [link](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr) | The IMF said Pakistan had restored macro stability, growth had rebounded, inflation had fallen, and reserves had doubled over the prior year. This is strong evidence that Sharif’s government managed a major economic crisis in a way that advanced state durability. | 8B.9
- **E0294 | PM unveils broader plan to sell most state-owned firms** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-05-14 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-unveils-broader-plan-to-sell-most-state-owned-firms/2084587/) | Sharif announced privatization of most non-strategic SOEs and framed it as saving taxpayers’ money and improving the investment environment. That is a regime-durability move through structural economic repair. | 8B.9
- **E0574 / E0708 | BISP digital-wallet rollout** | APP | 2024-03-18 | [link](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/) | Moving BISP payments to digital wallets reduced leakage and discretion. This is evidence of more rule-based state capacity, which supports durable governance rather than patronage. | 8B.9
- **E0571 / E0687 | Inquiry commission after judges alleged ISI intimidation** | Reuters via Al Jazeera | 2024-03-28 | [link](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/3/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says) | After judges alleged ISI intimidation, the government said it would form an inquiry commission. This is limited but real evidence that Sharif sometimes allowed politically sensitive investigations to proceed rather than bury them. | 8B.9

**Counterevidence**
- **E0005 / E0217 / E0277 | Election-day internet shutdown** | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08 | [link](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/) | Amnesty described the election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown as a blunt attack on expression and assembly. That supports a coercive, not trust-building, mode of managing political transition. | 8B.9
- **E0173 / E0211 / E0556 | Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09 | [link](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/) | Amnesty said the government rushed through a law that criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded powers to restrict gatherings. This is strong evidence of regime defense through legal suppression of opposition. | 8B.9
- **E0124 / E0174 / E0222 | Crackdown on PTI protests** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-09 | [link](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) | HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and internet cuts against PTI protesters, including peaceful demonstrators. That suggests Sharif’s government managed opposition through intimidation rather than durable accommodation. | 8B.9
- **E0143 / E0213 / E0553 | 26th Amendment and judicial independence** | The Guardian | 2024-10-21 | [link](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps) | Critics said the amendment weakened judicial independence and passed amid intimidation allegations. That cuts against preserving neutral institutions as a durable base for rule. | 8B.9
- **E0218 / E0501 / E0576 | X blocked on national-security grounds** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-17 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313) | The government confirmed blocking X around the election period. That is direct information control and weakens the case that Sharif managed scrutiny in a regime-stabilizing, institution-friendly way. | 8B.9
- **E0128 / E0151 / E0167 | Ahmadi community harassment and arbitrary detentions** | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21 | [link](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/) | Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and blocked religious rites, while authorities failed to ensure safety. This undercuts any claim that the state was reducing vulnerability or managing communal conflict well. | 8B.9
- **E0022 / E0043 / E0066 | UNGA Kashmir speech also used brinkmanship** | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | [link](https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute) | Sharif paired dialogue calls with hard-edged language about Indian military expansion and a “limited war” frame. That preserves leverage, but it also kept tensions elevated rather than cleanly de-escalating them. | 8B.9
- **E0142 / E0153 / E0569 | State Department on weak accountability** | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | [link](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128431.html) | The State Department said authorities rarely took credible steps to punish officials who committed abuses, while using media and telecom controls to suppress criticism. That is weak evidence for durable, accountable regime management. | 8B.9

**Search gap**
- I found strong coverage on 2024 coalition formation, IMF stabilization, diplomatic messaging, protest repression, media control, and court pressure.
- I did not find much direct evidence of Sharif personally resolving major crises through durable institutional bargains beyond official statements and top-down interventions.
- The biggest gap is independent, on-the-record evidence about internal civil-military bargaining and how much of the repression or diplomacy was personally driven by Sharif versus inherited state machinery.
